verbs.name: edit.split_edit
verbs.description: J-cut / L-cut (SPLIT EDIT): offset the AUDIO transition relative to the VIDEO cut at a clip boundary, so one clip's audio leads or lags its video -- the standard smooth-dialogue edit in every NLE. MODEL NOTE (see edit.detach_audio): a video clip's audio lives as a SEPARATE audio-track clip (the v1/a1t mirror), and clips trim/move independently. So a J/L cut is a ROLL of the AUDIO edit point against the (untouched) VIDEO cut, expressed as two ordinary edit.trims on the two linked AUDIO clips around the boundary. Because clip positions are CUMULATIVE, extending the outgoing clip's out-edge pushes the incoming clip's start later automatically and trimming the incoming clip's in-edge pulls its end back -- the net downstream effect is ZERO (a true roll), only the A|B audio boundary moves, the video is never touched. L-CUT (video leads, audio lags): extend A_audio out by offset_ms + trim B_audio in by offset_ms -> audio transition lands offset_ms AFTER the video cut (needs offset_ms of source past A_audio's out). J-CUT (audio leads, video lags): extend B_audio in EARLIER by offset_ms + trim A_audio out by offset_ms -> audio transition lands offset_ms BEFORE the video cut (needs offset_ms of source before B_audio's in). REQUIRES the audio to ALREADY be two clips butted at the cut (the natural distinct-sources state, each video clip with its a1t mirror). A single continuous audio clip across the cut has no audio transition to offset -> honest error pointing at edit.split / edit.detach_audio (the verb never silently splits the audio: that would allocate ids for zero semantic gain). v1 refuses a retimed (speed != 1) audio clip. Lowers to exactly TWO replay-safe edit.trim ops (no id allocation), grouped under one undo tag.

at_ms.description: The VIDEO cut position: the exact boundary (ms) between two adjacent video clips on the video track.

kind.description: "l" = L-cut (video leads, audio lags: audio rolls AFTER the cut); "j" = J-cut (audio leads, video lags: audio rolls BEFORE the cut).

offset_ms.description: How far (ms) to roll the audio transition relative to the video cut.

video_track.description: Video track holding the cut. Omitted = the base (first) video track.

audio_track.description: Audio track holding the two linked clips. Omitted = the first audio track that holds both halves of the butted pair.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {at_ms, kind, offset_ms, audio_a, audio_b, applied, audio_track, audio_boundary_ms, a_src_ms:{old,new}, b_src_ms:{old,new}} -- audio_a/audio_b are the two linked audio clips rolled; audio_boundary_ms is where the audio transition lands (at_ms +/- offset_ms); a_src_ms/b_src_ms are the before/after source windows (the only thing changed). Two grouped edit.trim ops appended.

verbs.name: edit.paste
verbs.description: Copy/Cut/Paste's PASTE half — duplicate a clip onto a track at a timeline position. THIN verb: it resolves a SOURCE clip to (asset, src_in, src_out) and LOWERS to edit.insert (the logged op is a self-contained edit.insert, so undo/diff/rebase already handle it — zero new core code). SOURCE: pass `clip` (the clip id to duplicate). SNAPSHOT FALLBACK: if `clip` is absent or no longer on the timeline, pass `asset` + `src_range_ms` so a clipboard snapshot whose source was deleted still pastes. `src_range_ms` (when `clip` is live) overrides the source window to paste a sub-range — REFUSED on a retimed (speed≠1) clip (the timeline→source mapping is non-linear there). KIND-CHECK (like edit.move): the source clip's track kind must match the destination track kind; caption clips are refused (use captions.*). RIPPLE: explicit `ripple` wins; omitted resolves from the destination track (base video/audio → true for AV sync, overlay/extra → false). LINKED AUDIO (`link_audio`, default true): when the source is a muxed VIDEO clip whose audio rides a sibling audio clip (same asset + same timeline start — the importer's linked-A/V signature), a SECOND edit.insert places that audio on its base audio track at the same at_ms (two ops, two undos). CURRENT LIMITS: insert-only (no overwrite), no effect/grade copy (a pristine duplicate), single source clip.

clip.description: Source clip id to duplicate. Optional: a snapshot paste of a since-deleted source uses asset + src_range_ms instead.

asset.description: Fallback source asset id, used when `clip` is absent or no longer on the timeline (requires src_range_ms too).

src_range_ms.description: Source sub-range [in,out] in ms. Omitted = the source clip's whole window. Refused on a retimed (speed≠1) source. REQUIRED for a snapshot (asset-only) paste.

ripple.description: Shift sibling tracks after at_ms by the pasted duration. Omitted = resolved from the destination track (base → true, overlay/extra → false), same rule as edit.insert.

link_audio.description: Also paste the source's linked sibling audio (a muxed video clip's audio on the base audio track) as a second insert at the same at_ms. false = the video clip only.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip_id, ripple, rippled_tracks} — the pasted clip (the video insert's shape), its resolved ripple mode, and the rippled siblings; op_ids carries BOTH the video and (when link_audio resolved a sibling) the linked-audio insert

verbs.name: edit.gain
verbs.description: Set audio gain in dB on an AUDIO-track media clip OR an AUDIO track (exactly one of clip/track required). Video tracks contribute pixels only; imported video sound lives on its linked audio track, so video/caption targets are refused instead of storing a render no-op. Absolute set; the op records the old value.

clip.description: Media clip id on an audio track

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {target, kind: clip|track, old_db, new_db}; one op appended

verbs.name: edit.fade
verbs.description: Set LINEAR fades on a clip or a track. Clip form: provided fields are SET (in_ms = ramp from silence/black at the clip start, out_ms = ramp to it at the clip end; clip-local durations that travel with the clip through ripples), omitted fields keep their value, explicit 0 clears that side; 0/0 clears the fade. Track form: a convenience resolved NOW — in_ms lands on the track's FIRST media clip, out_ms on its LAST (the 'fade the music bed in/out' gesture); recorded as plain clip fades, so re-run it after restructuring the track (edit.duck doctrine). kind selects streams: audio = afade only, video = fade only, both (default) = whatever the track renders; a kind that cannot render on the target's track (audio on a video track — video tracks contribute no audio to the mix; video on an audio track) is refused, never a silent no-op. Render: video fades dip to/from BLACK on the base track and ramp ALPHA on overlay tracks (the overlay dissolves over the base); fades longer than the clip are clamped at render time. Splitting a faded clip leaves the fade-in on the left half and the fade-out on the right (a mid-clip split never invents a dip). HONEST SCOPE: linear ramps only, per-clip; CROSSFADES between adjacent clips are a v2 feature — adjacent fade-out + fade-in (a dip to black) is the v1 approximation.

clip.description: Target media clip id (exactly one of clip|track)

track.description: Target track id: in_ms → first media clip, out_ms → last media clip

in_ms.description: Fade-in length, ms (0 clears). At least one of in_ms|out_ms required; in+out must fit inside the clip

kind.description: Stream selector; one kind per clip fade (setting a fade replaces the kind)

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {targets: [{clip, track, old_fade, fade}]} — one entry per touched clip (track form may touch two); one op appended

verbs.name: edit.mute_range
verbs.description: NON-DESTRUCTIVE mute range on one media clip — the low-level half of mute-word (transcript.mute_words resolves word indices to these ranges). Adds one [start_ms, end_ms) range in SOURCE-ASSET time (the same clock as src_in/src_out) to the clip's mute_ranges list (normalized: sorted, overlaps/adjacency merged), surgically UNMUTES an interval with remove_ms (subtracts it from every stored range — overlaps shrink, strict supersets split, other mutes untouched), or clears the whole list with clear:true. SOURCE time is the point: the mute stays glued to the spoken content through trims/slips/splits with no op rewriting (fades/keyframes are clip-local; duck windows are timeline-time and go stale — this deliberately is neither). The renderer gates the clip's audio volume to 0 over each range's overlap with the visible source window, mapped to post-speed segment time (reverse is mirrored correctly). Refusals: the clip must be a MEDIA clip on an AUDIO track (muting a video-track clip would 'succeed' inaudibly — target the linked audio clip or edit.detach_audio first); the range must be non-empty and intersect the clip's current visible source window; speed-RAMPED clips are refused (a piecewise mapping would drift the gate off the word). Fully undoable (project.undo) and replay-safe.

clip.description: Media clip id on an AUDIO track.

range_ms.description: [start_ms, end_ms) to mute, in SOURCE-ASSET time (the src_in/src_out clock — NOT timeline ms). Exactly one of range_ms | clear.

remove_ms.description: [start_ms, end_ms) to UNMUTE, in SOURCE-ASSET time — subtracted from every stored range (surgical; other mutes untouched). Exactly one of range_ms | remove_ms | clear.

clear.description: true = remove ALL mute ranges from the clip (the unmute). Exactly one of range_ms | clear.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: effect {clip, action: add|remove|clear, range_ms, mute_ranges: <the normalized resulting list>} — invalid_args when the target is not an audio-track media clip, the range is empty/non-intersecting, or the clip is speed-ramped

verbs.name: edit.transform
verbs.description: Set (or clear) geometry + opacity on a video clip. Normalized values are validated at the verb/core boundary: x/y = top-left corner as a fraction of frame width/height (0..1), scale = clip width as a fraction of frame width (0..1]; out-of-range values are rejected instead of clamped. Height scales proportionally (the clip is the full conformed frame, scaled). opacity = 0..1 alpha (1 = opaque). Identity (0,0,1,1) clears. LAYER CONTRACT: the first non-empty video track is the stable base canvas and every later video track composites above it in track order; empty tracks do not claim the base slot. Overlay transforms produce picture-in-picture over the lower composite. A base transform places/scales the picture over black, and base opacity (static or keyframed) blends against black. A hidden or gapped base remains black rather than promoting a higher layer. The same final transform/opacity stage applies after a base mask or power-window composite. The renderer only even-rounds/clamps already-valid pixel geometry to legal frame coordinates.

scale.description: Clip width as a fraction of frame width; 1 = full-frame

opacity.description: Clip alpha — 1 = fully opaque; overlays blend over lower layers, while the base blends against black; 0 = invisible

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.name: edit.crop
verbs.description: Set (or clear) a video clip's SOURCE crop rectangle (framing correctness). Values are SOURCE PIXELS (x,y,w,h) — the rectangle of the source frame to KEEP, NOT normalized — because crop happens in source space BEFORE the conform/transform stages. COMPOSE ORDER (contract): crop -> conform (scale/pad to project geometry) -> overlay transform (PiP); the renderer inserts crop=w:h:x:y as the first filter after the source trim, so the project frame is then filled with the cropped picture. Canonical use: remove a baked-in letterbox/pillarbox reported as the import's content_bbox perception fact (e.g. an OBS canvas/window mismatch that bakes black bands into the source pixels). When the asset is probed the crop must lie fully inside the source geometry (x+w <= width, y+h <= height) — out-of-bounds is a hard error; an identity crop (origin + full source size) clears it (stored as no crop). Applies to media clips on video tracks only.

x.description: Left edge of the kept rectangle, source px

y.description: Top edge of the kept rectangle, source px

w.description: Width of the kept rectangle, source px

h.description: Height of the kept rectangle, source px

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {clip, crop, old_crop}; one op appended (crop is null when an identity crop cleared it)

verbs.name: edit.grade
verbs.description: Native color grade on a media clip (the 'hero look' pass). Two optional stages, applied in order at render: PARAMETRIC (ffmpeg eq) then a 3D LUT (lut3d). Parametric knobs: contrast (1=unchanged), brightness (0=unchanged), saturation (1=unchanged, 0=greyscale), gamma (1=unchanged), temperature_k (white balance in Kelvin, ~6500 neutral, lower=warmer; omit for none). lut is a path to a user.cube 3D LUT (e.g. an S-Log3->Rec.709 conversion), applied last — the path must exist and end in.cube (we ship NO LUT files to keep the artifact license-clean; pro LUTs are user-supplied). An IDENTITY grade (all parametric defaults + no lut) CLEARS the grade (stored as none, renders byte-identical to ungraded). COMPOSE ORDER (contract): crop -> conform -> GRADE -> overlay transform; grade is per-pixel so it runs on the conformed frame. Media clips on video tracks only (audio/captions have no pixels). v1 is per-clip; track/timeline grade is a fast-follow.

clip.description: Clip id (a media clip on a video track)

temperature_k.description: White balance in Kelvin (~6500 neutral, lower = warmer); omit for none

lut.description: Path to a user.cube 3D LUT (applied last); must exist and end in.cube

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {op} — committed-op ride-along; the before/after grade is in op.effects[] (no bespoke top-level result fields)
